transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Any time I have to deal with those stronger cleaning chemicals, I either go out of my way to avoid them or push through it while feeling like I can’t stand being there. It has gotten to the point where it's really affecting my work, and my union representative suggested I come talk to someone.

When you’re around those cleaning chemicals, are you mainly afraid they will seriously harm your health, or is it more that being around them makes you intensely anxious or panicky even if you know they may not be dangerous?

It is definitely more of an intense, uncontrollable wave of panic rather than a rational worry about my health. Even when I know a cleaner is just a standard product that others use safely, just seeing a hazard symbol or catching the smell triggers a pounding heart, sweaty hands, and total dread.

Besides these cleaning chemicals, do you have the same kind of panic with other specific things or situations, or is it only with these products? Have you been avoiding places or tasks because of this?

It is strictly tied to these stronger chemicals and their smells, though lately I've even started avoiding some basic cleaners at home. To avoid them at work, I walk the long way to bypass certain supply closets, swap tasks with coworkers, and even call in sick on days they are scheduled. I've even turned down higher-paying routes and cut back my hours just to stay away from them.
